reasoning: Recent New Hampshire Senate polling in the last 45 days shows Democrat Chris Pappas leading Republican John Sununu by margins ranging from 1 point to 5 points, with the broader polling average at about D+5.4. The most relevant current-race sources therefore point to a Democratic edge in the New Hampshire Senate race, while New Hampshire’s statewide Cook PVI is D+3.0.

sources.name: NRSC / Peak Insights poll release
sources.details: Peak Insights found Chris Pappas and John Sununu essentially tied, with Pappas at 43% and Sununu at 42% in the New Hampshire Senate race.

sources.name: Pollsmax aggregate citing Saint Anselm College
sources.details: A Saint Anselm College poll included in the polling average showed Pappas leading Sununu 47% to 41%.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire survey as reported by ECIKS
sources.details: The University of New Hampshire survey reported Pappas leading Sununu 47% to 44%, a narrow Democratic edge.

sources.name: University of New Hampshire survey cited in Pollsmax aggregate
sources.details: The University of New Hampshire survey showed Pappas ahead of Sununu 49% to 42%, indicating a stronger Democratic lead earlier in the cycle.

sources.name: Pollsmax polling average
sources.details: The Pollsmax aggregate of 14 New Hampshire Senate polls reported an average of 46.7% for Pappas and 41.2% for Sununu, a D+5.4 margin.
